choices.text: Tell them to keep their distance

choices.text: Say nothing about it at all

effects.log: You say nothing about it, which is an answer, and they read it as one. It is a long age before the next prayer arrives.

choices.text: Answer, and ask after their light

effects.log: You answer, and ask after their light and spirits before anything else. It is a small thing that matters more than the intelligence.

events.text: Word comes, late and in a hurry, that {b3_agent} inside {b3_foe} nearly gave themselves away: a scribe-master who spots a changed word at fifty paces remarked on an inkstain in the shape of your own temple's mark in front of three witnesses. They talked their way out. They say so cheerfully, and the cheerfulness is how you know how frightened they were.

choices.text: Tell them to come home

effects.log: You tell them to come home, and they refuse, with polite stubbornness. You do not press. They have earned the right to be wrong.

choices.text: Send a warning and a remedy

effects.log: You send a coded warning, and a trick for hiding exactly that fault. The next prayer comes with a joke in it, and you feel better.

choices.text: Tell them to keep going

effects.log: You tell them to keep going, as the cause requires. It is easy to say. It is the sort of answer you reread at night and wish you had not sent.

events.text: {b3_agent} in {b3_foe} writes that they have made a friend there: a decent young god who shares the copy-room under the dome and suspects nothing. The prayer is careful. It is also, between the lines, a confession. They are asking you what to do without asking.

choices.text: Tell them to keep the friendship

effects.log: You tell them to keep the friendship, and to be honest in every way but the one that matters. It is advice you learned the hard way, and it is not good advice.

choices.text: Tell them to keep their distance

effects.log: You tell them to keep their distance, for the friend's good as much as their own. They obey, and the prayers that follow are shorter and colder.

choices.text: Say nothing about it at all

effects.log: You say nothing about it, which is an answer, and they read it as one. It is a long age before the next prayer arrives.

events.text: News from {b3_foe}: {b3_agent} has been praised for work as a junior scribe of their Book of Fates and offered a real post, with a niche and a title and a senior god's good opinion. It is a splendid cover. It is also a trap of kindness, because the better they do there, the harder the leaving.

choices.text: Tell them to take it

effects.log: You tell them to take it. The cover deepens, and so does the intelligence, and so does your guilt, in about equal measure.

choices.text: Tell them to refuse, modestly

effects.log: You tell them to refuse, with a modest excuse. They do, and the senior god thinks better of them for it, which was not the plan.

choices.text: Take it, and plan the exit

effects.log: You tell them to take it, and plan their exit together in the language of hymns. It is a long correspondence, and the plan becomes a kind of trust.

events.text: With the last prayer from {b3_foe} comes a chance: a page of their Book, copied from memory, with a name crossed out. Used well it would embarrass a rival, and perhaps endanger {b3_agent}, since only so many could have known. The prayer ends in the usual hymn, in the usual voice. Do as you think best.

choices.text: Use it, and cover the trail

effects.log: You use it, and cover the trail with three decoys. It works, mostly. A harmless god is blamed instead, which sits badly.

choices.text: Use only the safe half

effects.log: You use only the safe half, and leave the rest. It is a smaller victory, and you sleep.

choices.text: Burn it, and tell nobody

effects.log: You burn it, and tell nobody. It is the sort of decision that is never thanked, and you do not need it to be.

events.text: It is a quiet age at {b3_sect}, and the empty place in the front row of the Hall keeps drawing your eye. {b3_agent}, whom you sent into {b3_foe}, has not prayed, and you cannot decide whether that is good news. The eldest of the disciples has noticed, and is too polite to say so.

choices.text: Send a prayer in the old words

effects.log: You send a prayer in the old words, one line, asking only after the weather. The answer is slow, and the weather, it says, is fine.

choices.text: Wait, and say nothing

effects.log: You wait, and say nothing, and manage the waiting rather badly. It does not change anything, and it ages you a little.

choices.text: Throw yourself into the work

effects.log: You throw yourself into the work, and the Hall has never been so well supervised. The disciples find it both useful and unnerving.

events.text: Someone at the long table asks where {b3_agent} has gone, with the bright innocence of the truly unaware. Eyes turn. The eldest of the disciples studies the soup. Nobody takes it, and nobody says why, and you have a moment to decide what the Halls will be told.

choices.text: Tell the cover story smoothly

effects.log: You tell the cover story smoothly, a pilgrimage to the springs of the Green Assembly, and add details until it is nearly true. By supper it is.

choices.text: Say it is no one's business

effects.log: You say it is no one's business, in a tone that closes the subject and opens several others.

choices.text: Change the subject with a bad pun

effects.log: You change the subject with a pun so bad that three people leave the table. The question is not asked again.

events.text: You dream of {b3_agent} standing in a courtyard of the wrong pantheon, under a sky of the wrong colour, mending a lamp. They look up, and for a moment they know you are there. You wake with the empty place in the front row of the Hall in your mind, and a prayer of your own going up before you have chosen it.

choices.text: Spend the morning in stillness

effects.log: You spend the morning in stillness, sending the best of yourself along the long invisible line between you. Whether it arrives, you cannot tell.

choices.text: Dismiss it as a god's fancy

effects.log: You dismiss it as a god's fancy and take your tea. It is a lie, and a useful one.

choices.text: Write down every detail

effects.log: You write down every detail, as you would a campaign. An age later a prayer confirms the colour of the sky.

events.text: The ages roll on, and the cost of the long game begins to show in {b3_sect}. The eldest of the disciples is carrying too much, and {b3_agent}'s work falls to those who do not know whose it was. It is not fair, and you are the author.

choices.text: Share the burden yourself

effects.log: You share the burden yourself, taking the early watches and the dull ones. The others notice, and do not mention it, and it is the best thing you do all age.

choices.text: Give them a quiet feast day

effects.log: You give them a quiet feast day, and tell them it is a minor festival of the Court, which is almost true. They return in good spirits.

choices.text: Say nothing, and let it be

effects.log: You say nothing, and let it be. The resentment builds, and spends itself in an argument about a broom.

events.text: While the eldest of the disciples speaks of the empty place in the front row of the Hall, a rare sign comes from inside the other pantheon, not a prayer but a gesture: a particular grain of salt left on a particular sill. choices.text: Prepare for the worst

effects.log: You prepare for the worst, quietly, with a favour called in and a boat at the edge of the sky. Nothing happens for ages, and the favour is spent anyway.

choices.text: Signal that you are ready

effects.log: You signal that you are ready. The reply is a single grain, moved one place. It is, by their code, a thank you.

effects.log: You go there yourself, as a visiting pilgrim of no particular faith. You see nothing, and learn a great deal about how hard it is to look inconspicuous as a god.

events.text: On the first dawn after the binding, at the threshold of the domain, your youngest disciple stops short at the sight of the vast presence settled across the way in. The beast, {b3_beast}, does not stir. It has a slow, deep stillness that sets the temple bells humming. You have the vain feeling of being measured by something which has measured a great many gods before you, and found most of them thin.

choices.text: Greet it by name, formally

effects.log: You greet it by the name you gave it, with the bow due a senior. It inclines toward you, once, and the light about it shifts. The court exhales, and the matter is settled.

choices.text: Offer it a share of the offerings

effects.log: You offer it a share of the morning offerings, which it accepts with ceremony. Every witness tells the story, and each makes the portion larger.

choices.text: Leave it be, and keep watch

effects.log: You leave it be, and keep watch from a distance, as one does with an elder at rest. It is respectful, and faintly absurd.

events.text: A hunter of divine beasts, with a very fine net and a very poor reputation, has been seen on the star-roads near the domain. Your youngest disciple says the beast, {b3_beast}, was restless last night, shifting in its place, as if aware. The hunter's price has been rising among those who deal in such things.

choices.text: Drive the hunter off

ok.log: You drive the hunter off the borders of the domain, firmly, and the beast watches from the gate with mild approval. It stays closer to you after.

fail.log: The hunter slips past you, and it takes your beast a whole night to see them off. You are embarrassed in the morning, and the beast is gentle about it.

choices.text: Ward the gate with a domain-law

effects.log: You ward the gate with a small law of the domain, which takes an age of paperwork and a tithe. The hunter tries it once, and the beast watches him fail.

choices.text: Point them at a larger, stupider prey

effects.log: You send word of a larger, stupider quarry in a far domain. It is not nice. It works.

events.text: Your domain beast, {b3_beast}, is unwell. It keeps to the threshold of the domain through the age, its great stillness gone dim, ignoring the offerings and the praise. Your youngest disciple sits beside it, and your disciples take turns. A physician from the Green Assembly says it is simply age, and that nothing can be done, and does not meet your eye.

choices.text: Sit up with it through the night

effects.log: You sit up with it through the night, and say whatever comes to mind. By dawn it is breathing easier, and you are not sure which of you was being comforted.

choices.text: Go to the Green Assembly for a remedy

effects.log: You go to the Green Assembly and ask, humbly, for a draught for a beast. The old gods are scandalised and then charmed. The draught works, slowly.

choices.text: Ask it what it wants

effects.log: You ask it, plainly, what it wants. It does not answer, but at dusk it moves, with effort, to the highest place in the domain and watches the sun go down. You do not ask again.

events.text: The small child of a worshipper, carried up in a dream to the edge of your domain, has made a friend of the beast, {b3_beast}, and sits in the lee of it as in a warm harbour, singing. Their patron-spirit stands in the arch with a face that cannot decide between horror and awe. Your youngest disciple is trying not to laugh.

choices.text: Let the child stay where it is

effects.log: You let the child stay where it is. The beast makes a slow round of the whole court, very gently, as if the child were an egg. The patron-spirit faints, in the end, but gently.

choices.text: Lead the child out, gently

effects.log: You lead the child out, and the beast sighs and settles. The child sulks until morning, and the patron-spirit sends honey cakes for an age.

choices.text: Let the child dream here often

effects.log: You let the child dream here as often as it likes. The beast is never lonelier, nor the domain safer, than in those years.

events.text: A god of a rival domain tells you, over tea and with a great show of friendliness, that your beast, {b3_beast}, is smaller than the one their pantheon keeps. They describe it at length. You gather it has a voice of a sort you have only read about, and a dreadful temper. Your youngest disciple is not listening, and is taking notes.

choices.text: Lay out your beast's virtues

effects.log: You lay out your beast's virtues with the zeal of a recruiting clerk. It is not necessary, and not quite dignified, and the rival is quietly impressed.

choices.text: Agree, and ask to see theirs

effects.log: You agree, warmly, and ask to see theirs. The visit is arranged, and goes oddly well; the two beasts ignore each other with great courtesy.

choices.text: Change the subject to tea

effects.log: You change the subject to the tea, which is truly excellent. You are not drawn. The beast, when you get home, seems pleased with you.

choices.text: Say no, politely

choices.text: Say that it cannot be bought

choices.text: Say you do not know
